examples.title: custom: `aa_ppi.yaml` config + raw Hydra overrides
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/generate -F input_pdb=@target.pdb -F config_name=aa_ppi -F input_pdb_required=true -F 'contigs=A1-150/0 70-100' -F num_designs=10 -F 'extra_overrides={"ppi.hotspot_res":"[A59,A83,A91]"}'
examples.notes: Escape hatch for any inference config or override not exposed by the structured endpoints. See `rf_diffusion/config/inference/` in the vendored upstream source for the catalogue of configs.

request_fields.default_note: auto-select by the tool from the request inputs

request_fields.name: contigs
request_fields.description: Hydra contig string referencing residues in `input_pdb` plus stretches of length-only design, e.g. `46,A106-106,59,A166-166,2,A169-169,23,A193-193,46`. Bare integers are residues to be designed; `<chain><resnum>-<resnum>` are motif anchors.

request_fields.name: contig_atoms
request_fields.description: Per-motif-residue list of anchored atom names, keyed by `<chain><resnum>`. Each value is a comma-separated atom-name string. Example: `{"A106": "NE,CD,CZ", "A166": "OD1,CG"}`.

request_fields.name: ligand
request_fields.description: Comma-separated ligand residue names present in `input_pdb`, e.g. `NAD,OXM`. These atoms are kept in the scene as small molecules.

request_fields.name: contig_as_guidepost
request_fields.description: True = unindexed atomic mode (network picks motif residue indices). False = indexed mode (motif residue indices are fixed). Upstream demos default to True for the harder unindexed variant.

request_fields.name: only_guidepost_positions
request_fields.description: When `contig_as_guidepost=True`, restrict the guidepost set to these residues (others remain indexed). Format: `<chain><resnum>` or comma-separated list, e.g. `A106` or `A106,A193`.

request_fields.name: partially_fixed_ligand
request_fields.description: Per-ligand list of atom names to KEEP FIXED; the unlisted atoms are diffused. Format: `{"<resname>": ["<atom>", ...]}`. Example: `{"NAD": ["O7N","C7N"], "OXM": ["O3","C2"]}`.

request_fields.name: inpaint_seq
request_fields.description: Mask the sequence at these positions (auto-switches model to InpaintSeq where supported). Format: `<chain><resnum>` / `<chain><resnum>-<resnum>`.

examples.notes: Reproduces the `active_site_unindexed_atomic` demo. Set `contig_as_guidepost=false` for the harder indexed variant; supply `partially_fixed_ligand=<JSON>` and/or `only_guidepost_positions=A106` for the other three demo flavours.

examples.title: 150aa buried binder around PH2 with RASA conditioning
examples.curl: curl -X POST $URL/api/generate/small_molecule_binder -F input_pdb=@trimmed_ec2_M0151_NO_ORI_zero_com0.pdb -F contigs=150 -F length=150-150 -F ligand=PH2 -F rasa_active=true -F rasa_target=0 -F num_designs=10
examples.notes: Reproduces `small_molecule_binder_rasa_buried`. Lower rasa_target (0.0) → ligand fully buried in the binder. Set rasa_active=false to skip RASA conditioning entirely.

job_lifecycle.poll_recommendation: Poll the status endpoint every 5–120 s until status ∈ {'completed', 'failed'}. On failure, JobInfo.error_summary holds a one-line exception summary and error_tail holds the trailing ~4 KB of the subprocess log — usually enough for triage without a separate /log fetch.
job_lifecycle.restart_semantics: Jobs survive process and FC instance restarts via a `job.json` sidecar in each job directory. Jobs that were RUNNING at the moment of restart are downgraded to FAILED with failure_kind='interrupted'.

nas_layout.cross_instance_consistency: When multiple FC instances mount the same NAS at jobs_base_dir, all of them can see each other's jobs via read-through cache on GET. Writes (create/update) only happen on the instance that owns the subprocess.
nas_layout.cross_service_sharing: Other bioagent services mounted on the same NAS can read this service's output files directly by path, avoiding HTTP round-trips. Example: another service does `Path('/data/rfantibody_jobs/<id>/output/file.qv').read_bytes()`.

tool_outputs.note: Each backbone lands at output/design_<N>.pdb. The matching .trb file pickles the contig, the resolved config, and the input→output residue mapping. For the active_site endpoint the motif residues' sidechain rotamers are preserved; diffused residues are backbone-only (run LigandMPNN downstream for sequence design — see ProteinMPNN-server for an inline option).

input_uri_schemes.job://<job_id>/<filename>: Pull a PDB from a previous job on this NAS.
input_uri_schemes.file:///abs/path: Direct NAS path (shared across services on the same mount).
Generic HTTP(S) URL — incl. signed OSS URLs.

models.default: RFD_140.pt (set by aa.yaml). Pass `model=rfd_173` to override.

service_specific.paper_reference: Ahern et al. 2025 — "Atom level enzyme active site scaffolding using RFdiffusion2" (bioRxiv). Compared with RFdiffusion v1 (rfdiffusion-server), v2 handles ATOMIC motifs (sidechain anchoring) + small molecules; v1 handles RESIDUE motifs + protein-only PPI binders. Use v1 for ProteinMPNN-only sequence design pipelines, v2 for enzyme/ligand-aware design.

Stage a file on shared NAS and return a `file://` URI.

For inputs too large for the 128 KiB FC async event payload: upload the
bytes here over sync HTTP, then pass the returned `uri` as a `*_uri`
field on the real submit / async-task request. Because the file lands on
the shared NAS mount, any instance can resolve it later.

body.title: Body
body.description: Structured request body, useful for JSON endpoints. Files are not represented here.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: When an agent should reach for this example over the others.

EndpointExample.title: EndpointExample
EndpointExample.description: A copy-pasteable example for one endpoint.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One-line purpose (FastAPI route summary or first docstring line).

description.title: Description
description.description: Longer prose (FastAPI route description or docstring body).

operation_id.title: Operation Id
operation_id.description: OpenAPI operation id; agents can fetch /openapi.json and look up /paths/{path}/{method} for the full request/response schemas.

request_content_type.title: Request Content Type
request_content_type.description: Wire format the body uses: 'application/json' for plain JSON, 'multipart/form-data' when files are involved, etc.

request_schema_ref.title: Request Schema Ref
request_schema_ref.description: JSON pointer into /openapi.json (e.g. '#/components/schemas/Body_run_rfdiffusion_api_rfdiffusion_post'). Resolve there for the full schema; the flat `request_fields` list below covers the common case.

request_fields.title: Request Fields
request_fields.description: Top-level fields of the request body, flattened for agent consumption.

EndpointInfo.title: EndpointInfo
EndpointInfo.description: One service-defined HTTP operation, with enough metadata to construct a request.

FailureKind.title: FailureKind
FailureKind.description:
Coarse classification of why a job failed.

Set by `finalize_job` based on subprocess return code + output detection,
or by `reload_from_disk` when a job was RUNNING at the moment of restart.
Lets the client distinguish recoverable from fatal failures without parsing
`error_summary` strings.

name.title: Name
name.description: Field name as it appears in the request body / form.

type.title: Type
type.description: Human-friendly type name: 'string', 'integer', 'file' (multipart upload), 'array[string]', 'array[file]', or the name of a referenced pydantic model (in which case look it up in /openapi.json#/components/schemas).

required.title: Required
required.description: True iff the field must be present in the request.

is_file.title: Is File
is_file.description: True iff this is a multipart file upload — a scalar 'file' or an 'array[file]' (rather than a form/json scalar).

default.title: Default
default.description: Effective default when omitted: a literal (default_kind='literal') or a semantics token 'auto'/'unset'.

default_kind.title: Default Kind
default_kind.description: 'literal' | 'auto' | 'unset'. 'auto'/'unset' are semantics tokens (not sendable literals); 'literal' means `default` is a real value.

default_note.title: Default Note
default_note.description: One-line prose for the 'auto'/'unset' omission semantics.

FieldInfo.title: FieldInfo
FieldInfo.description: One request-body field, flattened from the OpenAPI schema.

failure_kinds.title: Failure Kinds
failure_kinds.description: All possible values of JobInfo.failure_kind (only set on failure).

poll_recommendation.title: Poll Recommendation
poll_recommendation.default: Poll the status endpoint every 5–120 s until status ∈ {'completed', 'failed'}. On failure, JobInfo.error_summary holds a one-line exception summary and error_tail holds the trailing ~4 KB of the subprocess log — usually enough for triage without a separate /log fetch.

restart_semantics.title: Restart Semantics
restart_semantics.default: Jobs survive process and FC instance restarts via a `job.json` sidecar in each job directory. Jobs that were RUNNING at the moment of restart are downgraded to FAILED with failure_kind='interrupted'.

JobLifecycle.title: JobLifecycle
JobLifecycle.description: Framework-provided job state machine. Identical across all bioagent services.

JobStatus.title: JobStatus
JobStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a job. Strings so JSON serialization is human-readable.

jobs_base_dir.title: Jobs Base Dir
jobs_base_dir.description: Root directory under which per-job dirs are created.

cross_instance_consistency.title: Cross Instance Consistency
cross_instance_consistency.default: When multiple FC instances mount the same NAS at jobs_base_dir, all of them can see each other's jobs via read-through cache on GET. Writes (create/update) only happen on the instance that owns the subprocess.

cross_service_sharing.title: Cross Service Sharing
cross_service_sharing.default: Other bioagent services mounted on the same NAS can read this service's output files directly by path, avoiding HTTP round-trips. Example: another service does `Path('/data/rfantibody_jobs/<id>/output/file.qv').read_bytes()`.

NasLayout.title: NasLayout
NasLayout.description: Where each job's data lives on disk; shared across multi-instance FC.

version.title: Version
version.description: Semantic version of the service image.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.description: Service-specific POST routes. Framework lifecycle routes are NOT included.

service_specific.title: Service Specific
service_specific.description: Whatever `adapter.manifest_extras()` returned. Services document their output filename conventions, supported input URI schemes, and any tool-specific hints here.

openapi_url.title: Openapi Url
openapi_url.description: Where to fetch the full JSON Schema for every request/response model.

ServiceManifest.title: ServiceManifest
ServiceManifest.description: Agent-facing protocol description for one bioagent service.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: Sanitized basename of the staged file.

path.title: Path
path.description: Absolute path on the shared NAS mount.

uri.title: Uri
uri.description: file:// URI resolvable by any service's *_uri input.

UploadInfo.title: UploadInfo
UploadInfo.description:
What `POST /api/uploads` returns after staging a file on shared NAS.

`uri` is a `file://` reference the caller passes as a `*_uri` field on a
later submit / async-task request, keeping large bytes out of the 128 KiB
async event payload.
